title: THE WORLD OF CRYPTOCURRENCY | History, Benefits, Risks & Uses
subTitle:
Cryptocurrency is no longer just a form of digital money. It has developed into a large ecosystem involving Blockchain, Smart Contracts, DeFi, Payments, Tokenization, and Web3.

But the big questions are: What was each major cryptocurrency created for? What are its benefits? What are its risks? And what should beginners be careful about?

🟠 1. Bitcoin (BTC) — The Beginning of Cryptocurrency

Bitcoin is the cryptocurrency that introduced the concept of decentralized digital money to the world. The Bitcoin whitepaper was published in 2008 under the name Satoshi Nakamoto, and the Bitcoin network launched in 2009.

Uses:
• Peer-to-peer value transfer

• Digital asset

• Global transfers

• Bitcoin ecosystem

Potential Benefits:
✅ Can operate without direct control from a central bank

✅ Can be transferred globally

✅ Users can control their funds through their own private keys

Risks:
⚠️ Bitcoin can be highly volatile

⚠️ Losing a wallet or recovery phrase can result in permanent loss of funds

⚠️ Transactions sent to the wrong address generally cannot be reversed

⚠️ Bitcoin is not completely anonymous; blockchain transactions are publicly visible

🔵 2. Ethereum (ETH) — The World of Smart Contracts

Ethereum was proposed by Vitalik Buterin in 2013 and launched on July 30, 2015.

Unlike Bitcoin, Ethereum was designed not only as a digital asset but also as a blockchain platform for Smart Contracts and Decentralized Applications (DApps).

Uses:
• Smart Contracts

• DeFi

• NFTs

• Decentralized Applications

• Token creation

Potential Benefits:
✅ Supports programmable blockchain applications

✅ Large ecosystem of developers and applications

✅ Major infrastructure for DeFi and Web3

Important Development:
In 2022, Ethereum moved from Proof-of-Work to Proof-of-Stake, changing how the network is secured.

Risks:
⚠️ Smart-contract scams and malicious contracts

⚠️ Signing a harmful transaction can result in losses

⚠️ ETH and other tokens can be highly volatile

🟡 3. BNB — The Binance Ecosystem

BNB is a cryptocurrency associated with the Binance ecosystem and is used across various blockchain-based applications and services.

Uses:
• Blockchain transactions

• DeFi applications

• Web3 ecosystem

• Various blockchain services

Potential Benefits:
✅ Connected to a large blockchain ecosystem

✅ Used across different Web3 applications

Risks:
⚠️ Market volatility

⚠️ Regulatory and ecosystem-related risks

⚠️ Like other crypto assets, it can lose significant value

🟣 4. Solana (SOL) — High-Speed Blockchain

Solana is a Layer-1 blockchain designed for fast transactions and scalable blockchain applications.

Uses:
• DeFi

• NFTs

• Web3 applications

• Blockchain-based payments and applications

Potential Benefits:
✅ High-speed blockchain architecture

✅ Growing Web3 ecosystem

✅ Supports a wide range of decentralized applications

Risks:
⚠️ Technical and network risks

⚠️ High market volatility

⚠️ New projects can carry scam and rug-pull risks

⚫ 5. XRP — Cross-Border Payments

XRP is a digital asset associated with fast value transfers and cross-border payment use cases.

Potential Uses:
• Cross-border transfers

• Payment infrastructure

• Digital asset transfers

Risks:
⚠️ Regulatory uncertainty

⚠️ Market volatility

⚠️ Speculative trading risk

🔵 6. Cardano (ADA) — Research-Focused Blockchain

Cardano is a decentralized Proof-of-Stake blockchain platform, while ADA is its native cryptocurrency.

Cardano focuses on areas such as research, scalability, sustainability, and security.

Uses:
• DeFi

• Digital identity

• Payments

• Tokenized assets

• Supply-chain applications

Potential Benefits:
✅ Proof-of-Stake blockchain

✅ Research-driven development approach

✅ Designed for decentralized applications and digital assets

Risks:
⚠️ Market volatility

⚠️ Adoption and ecosystem-development risks

⚠️ General cryptocurrency market risks

🐕 7. Dogecoin (DOGE) — From Meme Coin to Global Community

Dogecoin became famous as a meme-inspired cryptocurrency and eventually developed a large online community.

Potential Benefits:
✅ Strong global recognition

✅ Large community

✅ Has been used for digital tipping and payments

Risks:
⚠️ Meme coins can be heavily influenced by market sentiment

⚠️ Significant price volatility

⚠️ Buying only because of popularity can be extremely risky

🐕 8. Shiba Inu (SHIB) — The Meme Coin Ecosystem

Shiba Inu is another well-known meme-based crypto project that has developed an ecosystem around its community and blockchain-related initiatives.

Potential Benefits:
✅ Large community

✅ Expanding ecosystem

Risks:
⚠️ High price volatility

⚠️ Strong dependence on market sentiment

⚠️ Speculative trading risk

🟢 Stablecoins — USDT & USDC

Stablecoins are generally designed to maintain a relatively stable value compared with a reference asset, such as the U.S. dollar.

Common Uses:
• Crypto trading

• Moving value between digital assets

• Digital transfers

• Holding dollar-denominated value within the crypto ecosystem

However, stablecoin does not mean zero risk.

Users should also understand risks related to the issuer, reserves, regulation, depegging, custody, and platforms.

⚠️ Which Cryptocurrencies Can Be Risky?

It is not accurate to simply label a cryptocurrency as “good” or “bad” based only on its name.

The biggest risks often come from:

🚨 Fake projects

🚨 Scam tokens

🚨 Rug pulls

🚨 Pump-and-dump schemes

🚨 Fake investment websites

🚨 Fake crypto support accounts

🚨 Guaranteed-profit promises

🚨 Unknown links

🚨 Malicious smart contracts

🚨 Excessive leverage and futures trading

🛡️ Golden Rules for Crypto Beginners

1️⃣ Only use money you can afford to lose.

2️⃣ Never trust anyone promising guaranteed profits.

3️⃣ Never share your seed phrase or private keys.

4️⃣ Avoid unknown links and suspicious smart contracts.

5️⃣ Before buying a coin, research its project, team, tokenomics, use case, and security.

【原理】稳定币由发行方运营：你给它1美元，它发给你1个USDT，并把
美元（及等值资产）存进储备。市场上谁想把USDT换回美元，就向发行
方赎回。这套「申购-赎回」机制像锚一样，把价格钉在1美元附近。
价格偶尔偏离一点点（比如0.999），套利者马上搬砖抹平。

但历史上稳定币圈出过事——储备不够的稳定币脱锚崩掉，持有人血本
无归。所以：大额资金别长期躺在单一稳定币里，分散是免费的保险。

translatedData.subTitle:
You can’t trade futures without USDT, but many people have never wondered why it’s worth $1.

dollars (and equivalent assets) into its reserves. Anyone in the market who wants to exchange USDT back for dollars can go to the issuer to
redeem it. This “mint-and-redemption” mechanism acts like an anchor, keeping the price near $1.
The price may occasionally drift slightly (for example, to 0.999), but arbitrageurs quickly step in to close the gap.

translatedData.title: Trading Psychology | Staying Flat Is a Position Too—and It’s the One Experienced Traders Use Most
translatedData.subTitle:
The biggest misconception beginners have is that not holding a position means you’re not trading. So they stay fully invested, constantly buying and selling,
until fees and market swings wear away their capital.

In reality, staying flat is the only position with zero losses. If you can’t make sense of the market, stay flat.
Staying flat when bulls and bears are battling it out, and staying flat after a string of losing trades—the money you save at these three moments
is more than most people make from trading.

We’ve all heard the hunting metaphor to death, but the principle holds true: hunters spend most of their time waiting. Pulling the trigger
takes just a second. When you have capital on hand, you’ll have ammunition when an opportunity comes along. Hold on to your ammo.

translatedData.title: Trading Psychology | What Matters More Than Predicting the Market: Reviewing Your Own Trades
translatedData.subTitle:
Most people spend 90% of their time predicting the market and 0% reviewing their own performance. They've got it backwards.

Write down three things for every trade: why you entered (your rationale), what went right or wrong (execution),
and what you'll do differently next time (specific actions). Stick with it for a month, and you'll be amazed to discover that your losses
Your trade log is full of the same mistakes repeated over and over—for example, immediately reversing direction after a stop-loss,
or never holding on to winning trades.

The market changes, but your behavioral patterns won't change on their own unless you keep an eye on them and work to change them. The market is the most
honest teacher, and your trade history is your report card. Don't just look at your account balance—review your trading records.

But from a candlestick-chart perspective, the structure of this drop is very clear: yesterday, the 4-hour candle closed below the uptrend line. The downside breakout points to a target near $78,000, but for that target to be reached, the price first needs to break below the core support zone on the volume profile.

For now, price is still sitting right on this crucial volume support level. It has provided strong support several times before and is the most important support point in the current broader uptrend. Below it is the earlier weekly gap. If even that level fails to hold, then we’ll need to seriously consider a deeper pullback to between $70,000 and $80,000. But there’s a very positive signal right now: open interest rose by about 10% during this drop, while the funding rate has turned negative again. This means many traders are shorting at this level. Historically, when this combination appears after a decline—short positions build up and the funding rate turns negative—it often leads to a short squeeze.

There’s also a time-based data point worth watching: if the four-year cycle still holds, yesterday was precisely when Bitcoin’s bear market was expected to bottom. If this pattern holds, the price should only move up from here. translatedData.subTitle:
On emotional days, people forget every principle, so I wrote them down and stuck them up where I could see them:

One: Write down your stop-loss level before opening a position. If you can't write it down, don't open the position.
Two: Never risk more than 2% of your capital on a single trade. No exceptions.
Three: Never add to a losing position. Never average down.
Four: After three consecutive losses, stop trading for the day. Watch, but don't trade.
Five: Withdraw some of your profits. The money you take out is cash; what you leave behind is peace of mind.

Just five rules, and not one of them is about “how to read the market.” Because the reason people lose big money is never
that they misread the market—it's that their execution fell apart. Let's keep each other accountable.

Last year, a friend of mine got in with 10,000 U and rode a favorable market all the way up to 50,000 U. He was feeling great during that time, posting screenshots every few days. When people asked how much he’d made, he didn’t keep it to himself.

But the rebound never came, and most of the profit in his account disappeared. Later, when we were having dinner, he was still doing the math. If he’d withdrawn 20,000 when it was at 50,000, then even if the market kept falling afterward, at least that money would no longer be tied to the market.#ETH  

A lot of people are like this. When they’re losing money, they’re extremely cautious, but once they start making money, they get carried away. They turn 10,000 into 20,000 and think it could reach 30,000; once it hits 30,000, they set their sights on 50,000; and when it actually gets to 50,000, they start dreaming of 100,000. The thing is, the market doesn’t automatically make those 40,000 in profit yours just because you’ve earned them. As long as the money is still in your account, it’s still unrealized profit. So these days, my habit is simple: after a good run of gains, I take some money out. It doesn’t have to be a lot—even transferring a small portion of the profit is fine. I keep trading with the rest. If the market rises, I don’t regret taking some out; if it falls, I’m not as panicked. The market can swing back and forth, but it’s best not to let all your profits ride that roller coaster. The longer I’ve traded, the less I’ve cared about selling at the absolute top. What matters is how much you still have in your hands when the market is done.#MET

Everyone wants to double their money overnight, but the people who actually keep their money in this market are the ones who “get rich slowly.”
Let’s do the math: earning just 1% a day over 250 trading days in a year gives you 12 times your starting amount; earning a steady 10% a month
gives you 30 times your starting amount over three years. It doesn’t sound thrilling, but there’s something remarkable about it—it doesn’t depend on luck.

Doubling your money depends on market conditions; compounding depends on discipline. You have to wait for the right market conditions, but discipline is up to you. Don’t make your goal
“doubling your money this week.” Make it “making no major mistakes this week.” The money from the first goal is given by the market,
but the ability to achieve the second is yours. The market is open every day, but only those who preserve their capital get to keep playing.

translatedData.title: Trading Psychology | What does the candle you FOMO into usually look like?
translatedData.subTitle:
The price shoots up in one big bullish candle, everyone in the group is shouting “Buy!”, and you nervously jump in—only to end up
buying at the top. This plays out every day.

Take a good look at that big bullish candle that got your heart racing: it’s what fully invested holders are hoping you’ll chase in and take off their hands.
Chasing after a high-volume surge is essentially providing liquidity to those who were holding before you.

A simple but effective rule: when you feel like chasing, force yourself to wait for three candlesticks. If the pullback happens on lower volume and finds support,
you’ll get a better entry; if it drops straight back down, congratulations—you’ve saved yourself an expensive lesson. The market will always
give you a second chance, but it won’t give you your principal back a second time.

A lot of liquidations—90% of them—happen because people don’t know how to “roll their position.”

They think that if they make 1,000 USDT, they should use that 1,000 USDT to keep adding to their position. The more they earn, the bigger their position gets. Then they realize this approach may look like compounding, but in reality, it’s slowly pushing them to the edge of a cliff.

Once, the market was moving especially smoothly. I started with just 20% of my capital in the position. After the first leg up, I had a decent unrealized profit, and in a moment of excitement, I increased my position to 60%. Before long, the price suddenly pulled back. It was just a normal correction, but because my position was too large, my mindset changed instantly. I started watching the charts obsessively, adding to my position, and moving my stop-loss. In the end, I managed to turn a profitable trade into a loss. Only after that did I truly understand what it means to roll a position.#ETH 

It doesn’t mean adding to your position just because you’ve made a profit, or piling on more and more whenever you see the price go up. It means letting only the profitable part of your position take on more risk—but only when you’re right. For example, when I open a position now, I first think through the worst-case scenario. If the trade goes wrong, I take a small loss and exit. If it goes right and I have unrealized profits, then I consider using part of those profits to increase my exposure for the next leg. And every time I add to my position, I recalculate: if the market suddenly reverses, how much could I lose at most? If I can’t work it out, I don’t add. This habit has saved me many times.#MET 

The real danger isn’t a single loss—it’s continuing to pour money in after you’ve already lost. Rolling a position isn’t about making your account balance appear to grow faster. It’s about making the positions that are going right bigger and the ones that are going wrong smaller. Do you truly want to turn things around and get back on your feet?@Square-Creator-e6126298997b7

Beginner Lesson 5: BTC, ETH, and Stablecoins—Get to Know These Three First

The previous few posts covered security, depositing funds, spot and futures trading, and candlestick charts. Now that you’ve got the tools, let’s talk about the three types of coins you’ll encounter most often. No matter what altcoins you explore later, you’ll almost always come across BTC, ETH, and stablecoins. Learn to tell them apart first, and a lot of things will make more sense.

1. BTC (Bitcoin)
Bitcoin was the first cryptocurrency, launched in 2009 by someone using the pseudonym “Satoshi Nakamoto.” Its most important feature is a fixed supply cap of 21 million coins. New bitcoins are gradually produced through mining, and the amount issued is cut in half roughly every four years. The most recent halving was in April 2024.
Many people call it “digital gold,” mainly because its supply is fixed, it’s decentralized, and it has the longest track record. Its use cases are relatively limited, primarily transferring money and storing value.
In terms of market trends, BTC is basically the barometer for the entire market. When BTC takes a big hit, it’s hard for most other coins to avoid the fallout. That’s what we meant in the previous post by “don’t just look at an individual coin—look at the bigger picture.”

2. ETH (Ethereum)
Ethereum launched in 2015. Its biggest difference from Bitcoin is that it can run “smart contracts”—simply put, programs that run on the blockchain. Many of the DeFi projects, NFTs, and various on-chain tokens you hear about today are built on Ethereum or on chains compatible with it.
Any operation on Ethereum requires a transaction fee called a gas fee, which is paid in ETH. Fees can rise noticeably when the network is busy.
In September 2022, Ethereum completed “The Merge,” switching from mining to staking to maintain the network. Also note that ETH doesn’t have a fixed supply cap like BTC—this is something people often get mixed up.
In broad terms: BTC is more like a store of value, while ETH is more like a platform, with ETH itself acting as the platform’s “fuel.”

3. Stablecoins
Stablecoins are designed to keep their price pegged to $1. The most common ones are USDT and USDC. On exchanges, they essentially play the role of “dollars”: you use USDT to buy coins after depositing funds, to place orders, and to convert back into when you sell and want to reduce your exposure to risk.
Major stablecoins like USDT and USDC claim to be backed by reserves of equivalent value, such as U.S. dollars and Treasury bonds. But they aren’t bank deposits, don’t have deposit insurance, and aren’t completely risk-free:
- In March 2023, Silicon Valley Bank in the U.S. ran into trouble. Some of USDC’s reserves were held there, and its price fell noticeably below $1 for a while before recovering.
- UST, in May 2022, fared much worse. It was an algorithmic stablecoin that maintained its price through an algorithm and didn’t have sufficient asset reserves. It eventually collapsed completely, leaving many people with nothing.
So “stablecoin” only means that the coin is designed to have a stable price; it doesn’t mean there’s zero risk. Beginners should stick to major stablecoins and avoid chasing high returns with stablecoins from unknown sources.

4. The Most Common Beginner Mistake: Choosing the Wrong Network When Transferring Coins
The same USDT can be issued on several different blockchains, such as Ethereum (ERC20), TRON (TRC20), and BNB Chain (BEP20). When withdrawing or depositing coins, the sender and recipient must select the same network, and the address must match. Choose the wrong one, and at best you’ll have to go through the hassle of contacting customer support; at worst, your funds may be impossible to recover.
For your first transfer, we recommend sending a small amount as a test. Once it arrives, you can send a larger amount. Fees also vary between networks, so check everything carefully before confirming a withdrawal.

In a nutshell: BTC is the market’s barometer, ETH is the foundation of an ecosystem, and stablecoins are your “dollars” in the crypto market. Understand these three, and exploring other coins will be much easier.

Next time, we’ll talk about the difference between centralized exchanges and on-chain wallets. Which coin do you currently hold the most of? Tell us in the comments.

The content above is for educational purposes only and does not constitute investment advice.

新手第五课：BTC、ETH 和稳定币，先认识这三样

前面几篇讲了安全、入金、现货合约和 K 线，工具都齐了，今天聊聊最常碰到的三类币。不管你以后玩什么山寨币，基本都绕不开 BTC、ETH 和稳定币，先把它们分清楚，后面很多事就好理解了。

一、BTC（比特币）
比特币是最早的加密货币，2009 年由一个化名“中本聪”的人推出。它最核心的设定是总量上限 2100 万枚，靠挖矿慢慢产出，而且大约每四年产出量减半一次，最近一次减半是 2024 年 4 月。
很多人把它叫“数字黄金”，主要看重的就是总量固定、去中心化、运行时间最长。它的功能比较单一，主要就是转账和存储价值。
在行情上，BTC 基本是整个市场的风向标。BTC 大跌的时候，绝大多数币都很难独善其身，这也是上一篇说的“别只看单个币，要看大环境”。

二、ETH（以太坊）
以太坊 2015 年上线，和比特币最大的区别是它能跑“智能合约”，简单理解就是可以在链上运行程序。现在大家听到的 DeFi、NFT、各种链上代币，很多都是建在以太坊或者兼容以太坊的链上的。
在以太坊上做任何操作都要付手续费，叫 Gas 费，用 ETH 支付，链上忙的时候会明显变贵。
2022 年 9 月以太坊完成了“合并”，从挖矿改成了质押的方式维护网络。另外要注意，ETH 没有像 BTC 那样的固定总量上限，这一点经常有人搞混。
所以粗略说：BTC 更像价值存储，ETH 更像一个平台，ETH 本身是这个平台的“燃料”。

三、稳定币
稳定币就是想办法让价格锚定 1 美元的币，最常见的是 USDT 和 USDC。在交易所里它基本就是“美元”的角色：你入金买的 USDT，下单买币用的也是它，卖了币想先避险，也是换回它。
主流的 USDT、USDC 号称背后有等值的美元、国债等资产做储备，但它们不是银行存款，没有存款保险，也不是绝对不会出问题：
- 2023 年 3 月美国硅谷银行出事，USDC 有部分储备放在那家银行，价格一度明显跌破 1 美元，后来才恢复。
- 2022 年 5 月的 UST 更惨，它是靠算法维持价格、没有足额资产储备的那种稳定币，最后彻底崩盘，很多人血本无归。
所以“稳定币”只是说价格设计上稳定，不等于零风险。新手优先用主流的，别为了高收益去碰来路不明的稳定币。

四、新手最容易踩的坑：转币选错网络
同一个 USDT 可以在好几条链上发行，比如以太坊（ERC20）、波场（TRC20）、BNB 链（BEP20）等。提币或者充币的时候，发送方和接收方选的网络必须一致，地址也要对应，选错了轻则找客服折腾，重则直接找不回来。
建议第一次转账先转一小笔试试，到账了再转大额。不同网络的手续费也不一样，提币前看清楚再确认。

一句话总结：BTC 是市场的风向标，ETH 是生态的地基，稳定币是你在场内的“美元”，三样都搞懂，再去看其他币会轻松很多。

下一篇聊聊中心化交易所和链上钱包到底有什么区别。你现在手里拿得最多的是哪个？评论区说说。

以上内容仅为科普分享，不构成任何投资建议。

title: 盘口没动，成本在漂移
subTitle:
BTC 午后继续在 8.3 万美元附近反复，ETH 和 SOL 也没有给出很干脆的方向。很多人看到这种盘面，会觉得“没什么行情”，于是把注意力都放在图上：支撑还在不在、反弹有没有量、下一根线会不会突破。

但对合约交易来说，真正麻烦的地方经常不是图没动，而是订单环境在变。

今天这种磨盘最容易制造一个错觉：价格区间看起来很窄，交易成本也应该很稳定。实际不是。报价层会变薄，挂单会撤得更快，深度可能只在截图里好看，真正轮到你的订单进去时，成交价已经和你预估的价格不一样了。

这就是成交偏差最隐蔽的地方。它不像一次剧烈插针那样吓人，也不像方向判断错误那样明显。它更像慢慢漏掉的水：每一笔只多一点点成本，每一次只差几个最小价位，最后累计起来，利润空间被磨掉，风险缓冲也变薄。

尤其在流动性分散的时候，同一个交易对、同一张 K 线，可能对应完全不同的执行现场。

有的地方盘口第一层看起来够厚，但第二层、第三层断得很快；有的地方价差看起来很窄，但订单一旦放大，平均成交价就明显漂移；还有的地方规则设计不一样，触发条件、标记价格、成交优先级都会改变实际结果。

所以问题不是“BTC 会不会从 8.3 万美元这里反弹”。更现实的问题是：如果你现在要处理一笔订单，这一单到底会以什么环境成交？

很多交易者只复盘方向，很少复盘订单环境。看对方向以后，如果成交位置不舒服，追进去的成本更高，退出时的承接更薄，中间的容错空间就会被压缩。到最后，图上看起来只是小波动，账户里却已经变成一串不太显眼的成本漂移。

我更愿意把下单前的比较当成交易的一部分，而不是下单之后才抱怨滑点。先看报价层，再看深度，再看规则设计和预估成交价，最后再决定这一单从哪条路径走。方向判断解决的是“要不要做”，订单环境解决的是“做出来会不会变形”。

这也是我最近关注 PerpEX 这类执行比较视角的原因：它提醒交易者在按下按钮前，别只看价格图，也要看不同路径里的成交质量。磨盘不是没有风险，只是风险从方向波动，转移到了执行成本里。

#BTC #ETH

translatedData.title: The Order Book Stands Still, but Costs Keep Drifting
translatedData.subTitle:
This afternoon, BTC continued to fluctuate around $83,000, while ETH and SOL offered no clear direction either. Faced with this kind of market, many people think, “There’s not much happening,” and focus entirely on the charts: Is support still holding? Is the rebound backed by volume? Will the next candle break out?

But in futures trading, the real trouble often isn’t that the chart hasn’t moved—it’s that the order environment is changing.

A market grinding sideways like this can easily create an illusion: the price range looks narrow, so trading costs should be stable too. In reality, that’s not the case. The quote book can thin out, limit orders can be pulled faster, and depth may look good only in a screenshot. By the time your order actually gets filled, the execution price may already differ from what you expected.

translatedData.title: Trading Psychology | When You Hold on to a Losing Trade, Your Brain Is Lying to You
translatedData.subTitle:
What is someone down 50% looking at? The “all-time high,” thinking, “If it just gets back to my entry price,
I’ll get out.” Pay attention: this thought is all attachment and no logic. The market doesn’t know your entry price;
it only responds to current supply and demand.

Once you’re stuck holding a losing trade, you automatically seek out good news and block out bad news. This is called confirmation bias. You start thinking,
“This time is different.” Those five words have burned more money throughout history than any hacker ever has.

The antidote is simple in theory, but hard to put into practice: before entering a trade, write down exactly “what would invalidate the logic behind this trade,”
then act when that point is reached, regardless of how you feel. Separate decision-making from holding the position, and you’ll be able to see clearly.

translatedData.title: Trading Psychology | A Stop Loss Isn’t an Admission of Failure—it’s the Price of Admission to Your Next Trade
translatedData.subTitle:
Many people can’t bring themselves to take a stop loss because they see it as proof that “I was wrong,” and their pride
gets in the way. Try looking at it another way: a stop loss is insurance you bought in advance, and the premium is that small loss.
The difference between a professional trader and a gambler isn’t who’s more often right, but who allows themselves to be wrong.

The most consistent traders I’ve ever seen cut their losses more decisively than anyone when they’re wrong. Because they know: whether this trade is right or wrong
doesn’t matter. What matters is the expected value over a hundred trades. The next time your hand shakes as you’re about to stop out, tell
yourself: This is the price of admission, not a verdict.

title: 山寨季是怎么轮动的？为什么你的币总是最后一个涨
subTitle:
很多人难受的点：BTC涨的时候我的山寨不动，山寨起飞的时候我又没在
车上。其实山寨轮动是有大致剧本的。

【经典顺序】BTC先动（吸走注意力）→ 资金外溢到ETH和大主流 →
再扩散到板块龙头 → 最后扫到各种小币杂毛 → 全场普涨过热，行情
接近尾声。你总感觉自己的币最后涨，因为你买的位置往往就在轮动
链条的末端。

【两个实用观察】1. BTC占比（BTC.D）下降，通常说明资金在往山寨流，
山寨季启动的信号之一；2. 山寨普涨但BTC滞涨，往往是行情进入尾声
的信号，这时候追高杂毛币，接盘概率最大。

【结论】轮动不是平均主义，不是每个山寨都会涨。有叙事、有真实
流通量、有板块地位的才轮得到。与其猜哪个百倍币，不如盯紧资金
现在在哪、下一站可能去哪。

title: 滚仓：富贵险中求，还是爆仓加速器？
subTitle:
滚仓这个词最近很火，故事都一样：小本金几倍杠杆吃大趋势，滚动几次
翻几十倍。今天讲讲它没告诉你的部分。

【滚仓在干什么】浮盈不再落袋，而是当成新仓位的风险金继续开仓，
相当于拿市场的钱加杠杆。趋势不停，复利惊人；趋势一停，从浮盈
几十个点到归零，也就一两根大阴线的事。

【数学真相】滚仓的本质是「连续押对」。假设每次胜率60%，连对四次
的概率只有13%。你看到的一夜翻倍帖，背后是99个已经删号的人。
幸存者偏差是这个行业最贵的东西。

【如果你一定要试】1. 只用你亏光了也不心疼的那部分钱；2. 浮盈滚动
到一定倍数，强制抽出本金，用「市场的钱」继续滚；3. 提前写好清零
预案。滚仓是烟花，不是过日子。别拿过日子的钱，放烟花。

translatedData.title: Position Compounding: Fortune Through Risk, or an Accelerator to Liquidation?
translatedData.subTitle:
“Position compounding” has been all the rage lately, and the stories are always the same: use a small amount of capital and several times leverage to ride a major trend, roll it over a few times,
and turn it into dozens of times your original stake. Today, let’s talk about what they don’t tell you.

【What Position Compounding Does】Unrealized gains aren’t taken off the table; instead, they’re treated as risk capital for new positions, and used to keep opening trades,
It’s basically using the market’s money to add leverage. As long as the trend continues, the compounding is incredible; once it stops, those unrealized gains
can go from dozens of points to zero in just one or two big bearish candles.

【The Mathematical Truth】Position compounding is essentially “getting it right repeatedly.” If you have a 60% win rate each time, the odds of winning four times in a row
are only 13%. Those posts you see about doubling your money overnight come with 99 people who’ve already deleted their accounts.

title: EVERYTHING IS FALLING TODAY. BUT IS THAT REALLY BAD?
subTitle:
$BTC When the crypto market turns red, many traders panic.

But for a long-term investor, a market correction can also create an opportunity to accumulate strong assets at lower prices.

Right now, I’m paying particular attention to BTC, ETH and SOL.

₿ BITCOIN — THE FOUNDATION

Bitcoin remains the largest and most established crypto asset.

With a limited supply of 21 million BTC, deep liquidity and growing global adoption, Bitcoin continues to be one of the main assets to consider for a long-term crypto portfolio.

When BTC drops, I don’t only ask:

“Could it fall further?”

I also ask:

“Will today’s price look cheap 2–3 years from now?”

⟠ ETHEREUM — THE WEB3 ENGINE

Ethereum is much more than a cryptocurrency.

It is infrastructure for DeFi, stablecoins, NFTs, Layer-2 networks and thousands of blockchain applications.

For a long-term investor, ETH offers exposure to the broader growth of the Ethereum ecosystem.

◎ SOLANA — SPEED & GROWTH

Solana has built a strong position in the crypto market thanks to its high transaction speed, low fees and rapidly growing ecosystem.

SOL can be more volatile than BTC and ETH — but higher volatility also means potentially higher upside during a strong market cycle.

📉 WHY CONSIDER BUYING WHEN THE MARKET IS RED?

Because nobody knows exactly where the bottom will be.

Trying to catch the perfect bottom is extremely difficult.

A more disciplined approach is DCA — Dollar-Cost Averaging.

Instead of investing everything at once:

🔹 Buy a portion now

🔹 Keep some capital for another correction

🔹 Add more if the market confirms a recovery

This approach can reduce the risk of putting your entire capital into one price level.

💡 MY LONG-TERM VIEW

If your investment horizon is 1–3+ years, a temporary market correction doesn’t automatically change the long-term thesis.

For me:

₿ BTC = the core of the portfolio

⟠ ETH = exposure to Web3 infrastructure

◎ SOL = higher-risk, higher-potential growth exposure

🚀 Sometimes the best opportunities appear when the market looks the scariest.

But remember: a lower price does NOT guarantee future growth. Crypto remains a high-risk and highly volatile asset class.

Never invest money you cannot afford to lose.

👇 NOW I’M CURIOUS:

If you had $1,000 to invest for the next 3 years, how would you divide it?

Around $7.7, the support levels at $9 and $8 have been smashed one by one. The market is probably starting to say again: UNI is done for!

But today, I actually want to talk about something a lot of people may have overlooked.
Arc.
Uniswap has launched v2, v3, v4, and UniswapX on Circle’s Arc.
And more importantly, the protocol-fee extension for Arc has officially gone live. Fees generated by v2/v3/v4 can flow into TokenJar and, through the existing mechanism, ultimately be used to burn UNI on mainnet.

What does this mean?
When we used to talk about UNI, many people only focused on one question: How much trading volume does Uniswap have?
But now there’s another link in the chain:
Trading volume → protocol fees → TokenJar → UNI burn.
That’s what makes $UNI  increasingly interesting to me.
Of course, I’m not going to tell you right now that UNI will take off as soon as Arc launches.
There’s no need to.

No one knows yet how much real trading volume Arc can generate.
But the experiment has begun.
If stablecoins, institutional capital, and on-chain asset trading on Arc really take off, the market will get its first clear demonstration of how trading activity on a new chain can ultimately translate into UNI burns.

On top of that, whales have continued adding to their UNI positions during the recent pullback. Data shows that whales have added around 1.13 million UNI since September 28. But we should look at this objectively: whale holdings as a whole have yet to return fully to their early-September levels, so I wouldn’t spin this as “whales are going all in.”

With UNI down to $7.7 and market sentiment at its most pessimistic, we have an opportunity to ask: Has UNI’s story broken down, or are the people who bought between $6 and $10 simply taking profits?
Personally, I lean toward the latter.

There are just three things to keep an eye on:
Is real trading volume on Arc picking up?

Can UNI burns keep increasing?
If these three things start to materialize consistently, that’s when the market will truly realize how powerful $UNI ’s value-capture mechanism is.

title: A $99.8M ETH Long Is Within 4% of Liquidation: The $2,501 Line Traders Are Watching
subTitle:
ETH ETFs just saw a $202M outflow, and $596M of longs sit below $2,475. Here's how liquidation clusters work, and why they matter.

🚀 When Ethereum slipped below $2,600 on October 7, down about 3.9% over 24 hours, one number started circulating among traders: $2,501.38.
According to Lookonchain, via ChainCatcher, that's the liquidation price of a 39,025 ETH long held by a wallet tracked as Machi Big Brother. The position is worth about $99.8 million. With ETH near $2,598 at the time of the Binance Market Data report, that leaves roughly 3.7% of room (my own math).
📍 First, what "liquidation price" actually means.
A leveraged long is a bet made partly with borrowed money. If the price falls far enough, the position can no longer cover its losses, and it gets force-closed automatically at the liquidation price. For a long, a forced close means selling. That selling can push the price down a little more, which can tip the next trader's liquidation price, and so on. That chain reaction is what traders mean by a cascade.
So a liquidation price isn't a prediction. It's a trigger point, and big ones become levels that people watch.
👤 This wallet isn't new to this.
Lookonchain and other trackers have followed it through repeated liquidations over the past year, with losses in the tens of millions. It has often reopened positions afterward, sometimes by adding fresh margin. Figures vary by outlet, so I'm keeping that general. What matters here is the pattern: this is a trader who has run close to the edge before, which is why the $2,501 level draws attention.
🗺️ Now zoom out to the wider map.
Coinglass data, via ChainCatcher, shows what could be forced out on major centralized exchanges at two levels:
If ETH breaks above $2,715, about $1.44 billions of cumulative short liquidations could trigger.
If ETH falls below $2,475, about $596 million of cumulative long liquidations could trigger.
Two things stand out. First, the Machi liquidation price of $2,501.38 sits only about 1% above that $2,475 cluster (my own math), so the same zone is crowded from two directions. Second, the upside pool is about 2.4 times larger than the downside pool (my own math), while both triggers sit roughly 4.5% to 4.7% from the price at the time of the report. In theory, a push higher would have more fuel than a push lower. That's about how much could be forced, not which way price will go. Also, Coinglass tracks centralized exchanges, so I wouldn't assume this wallet's position is part of those totals.
🏦 The backdrop isn't friendly to dip-buyers, but it isn't one-sided either.
US spot Ethereum ETFs recorded a net outflow of $202 million on October 6, all of it from BlackRock's ETHA, according to ChainCatcher. The funds as a group still hold $17.356 billion in net assets, about 5.27% of ETH's market value, with cumulative net inflows of $13.549 billion. One heavy day doesn't erase that. It does show institutional demand isn't a one-way street this week.
The macro picture is part of it too. The 10-year Treasury yield closed Wednesday at 5.365%, it's highest since April 2002, and the Fed minutes pointed to another hike by year-end. Higher yields have been weighing on risk assets, gold included.
🧠 Why should anyone who isn't leveraged care?
Because cascades don't only hurt the people being liquidated. When forced selling hits a thin patch of the order book, the price can move faster than the news justifies, and that can shake out spot holders who place stops at the same levels. If you only hold ETH, your coins aren't liquidated. But a violent move around $2,500 can still feel very real.
✅ What this means for you
If you hold ETH without leverage, liquidation levels don't affect your position directly. They're a map of where volatility could spike, and a reason not to set tight stops right on obvious round numbers.
If you trade with leverage, treat this as a case study in buffer size. A cushion under 4% on a position this large leaves very little room for a bad day. Don't copy a whale's position because it's visible. A wallet shows what's open on chain, not the full strategy, since it could be hedged elsewhere.
If you follow on-chain trackers, remember that a liquidation price is a data point and not a forecast. Traders can add margin, reduce size or close at any time, and this wallet has done each of those before.
🟢 Calmer case
ETH steadies above $2,500, the wallet adds margin or trims, and the liquidation clusters stay untouched while the macro pressure eases.
🔴 Stress case
ETH breaks through $2,500, the position is force-closed, the $2,475 cluster is hit right behind it, and the cascade pushes price lower than fundamentals alone would.
👀 Three things to watch
1️⃣ The $2,500 zone
Does ETH hold above $2,501, or do the two liquidation points merge into one wave of forced selling?
2️⃣ The wallet's next move
Does it add margin, reduce the position, or let it ride?
3️⃣ ETF flows
Do ETHA and the other funds see further outflows, or does the Oct 6 outflow turn out to be a one-day event?
💡 The key takeaway
A $99.8 million long sitting a few percent above its liquidation price, in the same neighborhood as a $596 million cluster, turns $2,500 into a level the whole market can see. That doesn't mean it breaks. It means the move, if it comes, could be faster than usual.
The real question is whether ETH holds the line, or whether forced selling decides the next leg.
That is the part worth watching.

translatedData.content:
IMF releases $138 million loan, waives El Salvador’s excess Bitcoin accumulation

El Salvador’s loan negotiations with the International Monetary Fund have reached an interim outcome. Approved in 2025, the 40-month Extended Fund Facility (EFF), worth about $1.4 billion in total, includes provisions restricting the government’s accumulation of Bitcoin. El Salvador continued to accumulate Bitcoin beyond the permitted limits, however, at one point facing the risk of not receiving disbursements on schedule.

There are four key facts: First, the IMF Executive Board completed the country’s second and third reviews on October 1. Second, it approved an immediate disbursement of about $138 million (approximately SDR 101.96 million). Third, the IMF granted a waiver for the country’s previous failure to meet the requirements limiting Bitcoin accumulation. Fourth, the IMF said El Salvador had taken corrective measures and pledged to continue reducing the government’s involvement in Bitcoin-related activities. Going forward, it is expected not to accumulate Bitcoin beyond the scope of recorded donations, and to strengthen transparency disclosures on government-held crypto assets and develop the regulatory framework. Other reports say the IMF also called for an end to further Bitcoin purchase plans and the winding down of Chivo, the official crypto wallet project.

Breaking down the logic, the waiver is not unconditional approval. Rather, it is a combination of “acknowledging the breach, granting a waiver in exchange for corrective commitments, and attaching conditions to the disbursement.” The IMF has upheld the program’s discipline while avoiding an escalation of tensions that could result from a suspension of assistance. El Salvador has traded limits on further accumulation for liquidity—a clear policy choice. Notably, the waiver applies to past conduct; future accumulation is now limited to the scope of recorded donations.

The impact on crypto markets can be understood on three levels. First, the narrative of sovereign nations accumulating Bitcoin now has institutional limits. Government-led buying is likely to slow, although transparency requirements may improve the quality of holdings disclosures. Second, winding down official projects such as Chivo signals a shift in the state’s crypto involvement from expansion to retrenchment and standardization. Third, the constraints multilateral institutions can place on members’ crypto policies have been reaffirmed. Other countries seeking similar assistance may face comparable requirements if they hold Bitcoin.

It is important to distinguish facts from speculation: the disbursement amount, waiver decision, and commitments are all supported by official disclosures. The idea that “slower sovereign buying will affect Bitcoin supply and demand,” however, is a logical inference; the actual effect will also depend on macroeconomic conditions and market sentiment. In the editor’s view, this outcome weakens the near-term prospect of “continued accumulation by states,” but bringing government holdings into a more transparent framework may not be a bad thing for the industry’s long-term standardization.

content:
IMF放行1.38亿美元贷款，豁免萨尔瓦多比特币增持超限

萨尔瓦多与国际货币基金组织的贷款博弈有了阶段性结果。2025年获批的这项为期40个月、总规模约14亿美元的扩展基金安排（EFF），包含限制政府积累比特币的条款；此后萨尔瓦多仍在法定许可范围之外继续增持，一度面临无法按期获得放款的风险。

核心事实有四点：其一，IMF执行董事会于10月1日完成对该国的第二轮与第三轮审查；其二，批准约1.38亿美元（约1.0196亿特别提款权）的即时拨付；其三，针对此前未满足比特币积累限制要求的情况，IMF批准了豁免；其四，IMF表示萨尔瓦多已采取纠正措施，承诺继续降低政府在比特币相关活动中的参与度，后续预计不再进行超出已记录捐赠范围之外的比特币积累，并将加强政府持有加密资产的透明度披露与监管框架建设。另有报道称，IMF同时要求停止进一步的比特币购买计划，并清理官方加密钱包项目Chivo。

逻辑上拆解，豁免并非无条件放行，而是「承认超限事实＋以纠正承诺换取豁免＋拨付附带约束」的组合处理。IMF既维护了项目纪律，也避免了援助中断引发的博弈升级；萨尔瓦多以限制增持换取流动性，属于明确的政策取舍。值得注意的是，豁免针对的是既往行为，未来的增持空间已被限定在已记录捐赠范围之内。

对加密市场的影响路径可从三个层面理解。第一，主权国家增持比特币的叙事被加上制度边界，政府主导的买入节奏大概率放缓，但透明度要求可能反而提升持仓披露质量；第二，Chivo等官方项目的清理，意味着国家层面的加密触角从扩张转向收缩与规范化；第三，多边机构对成员国加密政策的约束力得到确认，其他寻求类似援助的国家若配置比特币，可能面对相似模板。

需要区分事实与推测：拨付金额、豁免决定与各项承诺均有官方披露支撑；而「主权买入放缓影响比特币供需」属于逻辑推演，实际效果还取决于宏观环境与市场情绪。编辑观察认为，这一结果短期内弱化了「国家持续增持」的想象空间，但把政府持仓纳入更透明的框架，对行业长期规范化未必是坏事。

One Company Owns Nearly 5% of All Ethereum — And They Just Announced They're Stopping

For 15 straight months, one buyer kept absorbing Ethereum off the market every single week. That's about to end.

BitMine Immersion Technologies now holds 6,016,414 ETH — roughly 4.9% of the entire circulating supply — after Chairman Tom Lee announced at Token2049 in Singapore that 5% is a hard, non-negotiable ceiling. "That's a hard cap. We're not gonna be accumulating past 5%," Lee said directly.

Here's the scale of what's ending: BitMine made recurring weekly purchases throughout this run — a single 101,627 ETH buy in April, another 76,881 ETH in June, and 15,112 ETH just last week alone. It became one of the clearest, most consistent sources of institutional spot demand Ethereum has had.

They need roughly 100,000 more ETH, worth about $250-270 million, before accumulation fully stops.

Lee's own reasoning for the cap is worth sitting with: stopping purchases means BitMine no longer needs to raise fresh capital to keep buying, which he argues lets the company's stock outperform ETH itself on the way up, since investors won't need to worry about dilution from future raises.

$ETH  actually fell about 5% to $2,564 following the announcement — the market's immediate read was "one of the biggest buyers is stepping back," not celebration.

The honest question this leaves hanging: once BitMine's reliable weekly demand disappears, does something else — ETFs, other treasuries, organic adoption — actually step up to fill that gap, or does Ethereum lose a demand floor it's quietly leaned on for over a year?

Does ETH's price reaction tell you the market already depended on BitMine more than anyone admitted, or is this a short-term overreaction to otherwise good long-term news? 👇

subTitle:
如果你看不懂复杂技术，又想判断哪个 Layer2 更值得跟踪，别急着在 $ARB、$OP 之间凭感觉二选一。

普通人真正需要的不是“谁会涨”的答案，而是一把统一的尺子。L2BEAT 就适合干这件事：把 Layer2 的规模、风险和活跃度放在同一套框架里比较。

第一步，看 TVL，但别只看绝对数字。

更重要的是观察趋势：锁仓价值是在持续增加，还是靠短期活动突然冲高；资产构成是否集中，增长能否延续。TVL 上升代表更多资金进入协议，但不等于代币价格一定上涨，还要继续验证真实使用情况。

第二步，切到 Risk 页面。

重点看状态验证、数据可用性、升级权限和故障退出机制。这里解决的不是“会不会涨”，而是“极端情况下，用户能否验证状态、取回资产，项目方权限是否过大”。

安全项表现较好，也不代表完全没有风险。L2BEAT 给的是技术风险框架，不能替代对团队、代币经济和市场流动性的判断。

第三步，看 Activity。

交易笔数、吞吐量等数据，可以帮你区分“资金进来了”和“用户真的在用”。如果一个项目 TVL 増长，链上活动也同步提升，关注价值通常比只靠叙事拉动的项目更高。

具体研究时，再点进项目详情，把 TVL、活跃度和风险变化放在一起看。你寻找的不是某个单日暴涨的数据，而是多个指标连续一段时间同向改善。

L2BEAT 不能替你选币，但能帮你少做一次只看价格、只听故事的决定。今天就挑一个关注中的 Layer2，用这三步重新检查一遍。

title: 2%仓位法则：为什么亏得起才能活得久
subTitle:
今天讲一个被讲烂了但99%的人做不到的规矩：单笔交易的最大亏损，
不要超过总资金的2%。

【算笔账】1万U本金，2%就是单笔最多亏200U。连续错10次，还剩八千，
账户只回撤20%，靠几笔对的单就能回来。反过来，每次梭哈亏30%，
连错三次只剩34%，要翻近2倍才能回本——数学上已经基本判死刑了。

【怎么落地】不是「仓位不超过2%」，是「这笔单打到止损位时亏的钱
不超过2%」。所以正确顺序是：找止损位 → 算止损距离 → 反推仓位。
止损远的单仓位小，止损近的单仓位可以适当放大。

【为什么难】因为2%赚得太慢，人性嫌它不够刺激。但市场淘汰的从来
不是赚得慢的人，是亏得快的人。先做到不爆仓，再谈翻倍。

translatedData.title: The 2% Position Sizing Rule: Why You Need to Be Able to Afford Losses to Last
translatedData.subTitle:
Today, let’s talk about a rule that’s been repeated to death but that 99% of people can’t follow: the maximum loss on any single trade
should not exceed 2% of your total capital.

【Let’s do the math】With 10,000 U in capital, 2% means a maximum loss of 200 U per trade. After 10 consecutive losses, you’d still have 8,000,
With just a 20% drawdown, a few winning trades can get your account back on track. By contrast, if you go all-in and lose 30% each time,
three losses in a row leave you with just 34% of your capital. You’d need to nearly double it just to break even—the math has basically sentenced you to death.

【How to put it into practice】It’s not “keep your position size under 2%.” It’s “make sure the amount you’d lose if this trade hits its stop-loss
is no more than 2%.” So the right order is: find the stop-loss level → calculate the stop-loss distance → work backward to determine your position size.

Do you know why, in recent years, more and more men are starting to care about fitness?

For a long time, the core capability by which men solve problems was abstract ability—that is, what we usually call “intelligence.”

Besides reproduction, men have established very clear advantages in most competitive areas of human society by relying on physical strength, intelligence, and organizational ability.

But AI is changing all of that.

In the past, it might take a man ten or twenty years to accumulate knowledge, experience, logic, and analytical skills. Now, he may only need to call on an AI.

When abstract ability is no longer scarce, men’s most important competitive advantage in the past begins to be re-priced.

So you’ll notice a very interesting phenomenon:

More and more men are starting to work out, shape their bodies, study posture, and even become re-obsessed with their own bodies.

They call it “for health.”

Of course, it’s true.

But on a larger civilizational scale, it may also be a kind of forced acceptance.

Because as AI begins to take over more and more of the abstract world, the things humans can truly control are increasingly concentrated in their own physical bodies.

In the past, men proved themselves through their minds.

In the future, men may start proving themselves again through their bodies.

Not because the body has suddenly become more important.

But because intelligence is gradually shifting from humanity’s scarcest resource into a kind of basic infrastructure that can be called upon anytime.

Night of a Liquidation

At 3:17 a.m., the cold glow from his phone screen washed over Chen Mo’s face.

ETH, 2435.

He stared at the number. What reflected in his pupils was not the candlestick chart, but the string of margin balance in his account as it plummeted. Three days ago, Ethereum was still above 2700. Confidently, he posted in the group: “This ETH run is going to break 3000,” and then went long with 20x leverage.

Fifty thousand U—full position.

Back then, he thought he was a genius. Last month, he shorted PEPE and made thirty thousand. The month before that, he bottom-picked STRK and doubled his money. A streak of success created a kind of illusion—he believed he could really predict the market. His fellow group members called him “Chen God.” He waved it off with a laugh, but secretly he felt the title was well deserved.

But the market never indulges anyone.

When the first big bearish candle slammed down, he was still eating instant noodles. His chopsticks hung in midair as the price slid from 2680 all the way to 2580. He told himself, “A normal pullback. Don’t panic.”

The second bearish candle appeared two hours later. 2500 broke. His unrealized loss had already exceeded forty percent of his principal. His fingers began to tremble, but he didn’t set a stop-loss. “It’ll come back,” he said to himself. “Every big drop is just a washout.”

Then BTC couldn’t hold either. 83,000. 82,000. 81,000. The whole market felt like its backbone had been yanked out, and all the altcoins followed the waterfall-like plunge. OGN fell to nearly half. RLC wasn’t spared either. His ETH long position, opened around 2450, received its first warning—red exclamation marks on the screen flashed like crazy.

He added margin.

Then it fell again.

Second warning. Third. The phone started vibrating—the contract group messages were flooding nonstop. Some people shouted “buy the dip,” some cursed “the market maker,” and someone posted a falling-to-your-death meme.

At 3:17 a.m., ETH fell to 2435.

His position was forcibly liquidated.

A line of icy text popped up on the screen: Your position has been liquidated. 50,000 USDT—zeroed out.

Chen Mo put down his phone. The room was so quiet he could hear the refrigerator humming. The noodles had gone cold, but he had no appetite. He opened WeChat—the contract group messages were still streaming—but he couldn’t take in a single word.

He remembered three months ago, when he opened his first futures trade. He only dared to use 1,000 U as a test. He earned fifty bucks and was so excited he couldn’t contain himself. Back then, he understood to respect the market. He knew how to set stop-losses. He knew how to manage position size.

But after making money, respect turned into greed; caution turned into arrogance.

He turned off his phone and lay back on the bed. In the darkness, the ceiling blurred into a gray smear. He knew tomorrow’s sun would rise and the market would open again—but he also knew he would need a long time to get over the lesson from that night.

Fifty thousand yuan—wasn’t the biggest money he had ever made or lost. But what that night taught him was more expensive than any course.

Never go all-in leverage without a stop-loss. Never think you can’t lose after a string of wins.

The market is always right; the only one wrong is you.

content:
爆仓之夜

凌晨三点十七分，手机屏幕的冷光打在陈默脸上。

ETH，2435。

他盯着这个数字，瞳孔里映着的不是K线，而是自己账户里那串正在跳水的保证金余额。三天前，以太坊还在2700上方，他信誓旦旦地在群里说"ETH这波要冲3000"，然后开了20倍杠杆做多。

五万U，全仓。

那时候他觉得自己是天才。上个月做空PEPE赚了三万，上上个月抄底STRK翻了一倍，连续的成功让他产生了一种幻觉，以为自己真的能预判市场。群友喊他"陈神"，他笑着摆手，心里却觉得这个称号当之无愧。

可市场从不惯着任何人。

第一根大阴线砸下来的时候，他还在吃泡面。筷子悬在半空，看着价格从2680一路滑到2580，他安慰自己：正常回调，别慌。

第二根阴线出现在两小时后。2500破了。他的未实现亏损已经超过了本金的百分之四十。手指开始发抖，但他没有设止损。"会回来的"，他对自己说，"每次大跌都是洗盘。"

然后BTC也撑不住了。八万三，八万二，八万一。整个市场像被抽掉了脊梁骨，所有山寨币跟着瀑布式下坠。OGN跌了快一半，RLC也没能幸免。他的ETH多单在2450的时候收到了第一条预警，红色感叹号在屏幕上疯狂闪烁。

他充了保证金。

又跌。

第二条预警。第三条。手机开始震动，是合约群里的消息在刷屏。有人喊"抄底"，有人骂"庄家"，有人发了个跳楼的表情包。

凌晨三点十七分，ETH跌到2435。

他的仓位被强制平仓了。

屏幕上弹出那行冰冷的文字：您的持仓已被清算。五万USDT，归零。

陈默放下手机，房间安静得能听见冰箱的嗡嗡声。泡面已经凉了，他却没有胃口。打开微信，合约群的消息还在刷屏，但他一个字也看不进去。

他想起三个月前，自己第一次开合约的时候，只敢用一千U试水，赚了五十块就激动得不行。那时候他懂得敬畏市场，懂得设止损，懂得仓位管理。

可赚钱之后，敬畏就变成了贪婪，谨慎就变成了自负。

V神也开始关注到 OpenAI 在数学领域的突破。

整个加密市场真正开始恐慌的，其实已经不是“AI 会不会破解公钥密码学”。

而是一个更可怕的问题，AI 到底什么时候能够破解？以前我们讨论密码学安全，默认的是数学问题足够难，人类算力永远不够。但 AI 正在改变这个前提。

OpenAI 这次一次性释放数百项数学研究成果，本质上是在告诉人类，AI 开始从“使用数学”，逐渐走向“发现新的数学”。而密码学的安全，本身就是建立在某些数学问题足够难的基础上。

所以这件事情对加密市场最大的冲击，并不是今天有人突然可以盗走你的 比特币、以太坊，而是市场第一次开始认真意识到，公钥密码学的安全性，也许不是永恒的。

看到OpenAi破解722道数学题时就感觉很炸裂，而且有“修改”部分作品。

压力真的给到了公钥密码学，也许未来有一天会突然出现一些Ai攻破公钥密码学谣言造成实质性的“恐慌，也许会出现真正的攻破。

中本聪的比特币貌似真的处于一种不太安全的“安全状态”。

加密市场的安全始终建立在“数学安全的高地上”，过去担心量子计算，但现在Ai展现的数学能力，远比量子计算更让人感觉恐慌。

整个文明曲线已经被722道数学题拖入一个科技大爆炸的时代，数学问题解决后、很快就是物理学、化学、生物学、以及一些超级材料的制造。

subTitle:
Uptober মার্কেট আপডেট: RSI ও MACD সিগন্যালে শীর্ষ ৫ ক্রিপ্টোর লাইভ স্ন্যাপশট ও ট্রেডিং গাইড!
ক্রিপ্টোকারেন্সি মার্কেট ২০২৬ সালের অক্টোবর মাসে এসে একটি অত্যন্ত গুরুত্বপূর্ণ টেকনিক্যাল মোড়ে অবস্থান করছে KuCoin News। ঐতিহাসিক ট্রেন্ড অনুযায়ী "Uptober" বা অক্টোবরের বুলিশ মোমেন্টাম ধরে রাখতে শীর্ষ কয়েনগুলো তাদের প্রধান রেজিস্ট্যান্স জোন ভাঙার চেষ্টা করছে।
মার্কেট ট্রেন্ড এবং মোমেন্টাম নিখুঁতভাবে বুঝতে আজকের ব্লগে আমরা ব্যবহার করেছি দুটি জনপ্রিয় ইন্ডিকেটর: RSI ( Relative Strength Index)—যা মার্কেট ওভারবট নাকি ওভারসোল্ড তা দেখায়, এবং MACD (Moving Average Convergence Divergence)—যা ট্রেন্ডের শক্তি ও দিক নিশ্চিত করে। [[1](https://www.binance.com/en/square/post/17639474109170), [2](https://www.binance.com/en/square/post/22980686843049)]
চলুন শীর্ষ ৫টি ক্রিপ্টো অ্যাসেটের বর্তমান টেকনিক্যাল সিগন্যালসহ লাইভ স্ন্যাপশট দেখে নেওয়া যাক:

 শীর্ষ ক্রিপ্টো কয়েনসমূহের লাইভ টেকনিক্যাল স্ন্যাপশট
নিচে আজকের বাজারের লাইভ প্রাইস অ্যাকশন এবং প্রধান ইন্ডিকেটরগুলোর অবস্থা তুলে ধরা হলো:
টোকেনলাইভ প্রাইস (USD)*RSI (14) সিগন্যালMACD (12, 26, 9) সিগন্যালটেকনিক্যাল আউটলুক ও অ্যাকশনBitcoin (BTC)$৮০,৮৪০+২৮ (ওভারসোল্ড জোন)বেরিশ ক্রসওভারস্বল্পমেয়াদে কারেকশন চলছে, তবে বড় ট্রেন্ড বুলিশ।Ethereum (ETH)$২,৫৫০+৪৩ (নিউট্রাল)নিউট্রাল / ফ্ল্যাট মোমেন্টামETH/BTC ব্রেকআউটের জন্য শক্তি সঞ্চয় করছে।Binance Coin (BNB)$৭৬৫+৫৩ (বুলিশ নিউট্রাল)বুলিশ মোমেন্টামইকোসিস্টেমের নতুন আপগ্রেডের কারণে শক্তিশালী পজিশন [Binance Square Insights](https://www.binance.com/en/square/post/23930412674841)।Solana (SOL)$১১৫.২০৫৪.১২ (নিউট্রাল)বাই সিগন্যাল (স্বল্পমেয়াদী)মেমকয়েন ভলিউম এবং মেইননেট আপগ্রেডের প্রভাবে গতিশীল।Zcash (ZEC)$১,২৪১৪৫ (নিউট্রাল)সামান্য বেরিশ / কনসোলিডেশনETF ফান্ড আউটফ্লোর কারণে কিছুটা বিক্রেতাদের চাপে রয়েছে।
*দ্রষ্টব্য: ক্রিপ্টো মার্কেট অত্যন্ত পরিবর্তনশীল, লাইভ ডেটা চার্টের সাথে মূল্য ও ইন্ডিকেটর দ্রুত পরিবর্তিত হতে পারে।

 ইন্ডিকেটর ভিত্তিক গভীর বাজার বিশ্লেষণ (Deep Dive Technical Analysis)
১. Bitcoin ($BTC): কারেকশন নাকি বাউন্স ব্যাক?
বিটকয়েন বর্তমানে $৮০,০০০ লেভেলের উপরে ট্রেড হচ্ছে। ৪ ঘণ্টার চার্টে শর্ট-টার্ম প্রফিট বুকিংয়ের কারণে RSI বর্তমানে ২৮-এ নেমে এসেছে, যা একটি ওভারসোল্ড পরিস্থিতি নির্দেশ করে। পাশাপাশি MACD-তে একটি বেরিশ ক্রসওভার দেখা যাচ্ছে। টেকনিক্যাল নিয়ম অনুযায়ী, ওভারসোল্ড RSI থেকে যেকোনো সময় একটি শার্প বাউন্স ব্যাক (Rebound) আসতে পারে, যদি প্রাতিষ্ঠানিক সাপোর্ট লেভেল বজায় থাকে। [1, 2, [3](https://www.binance.com/en/square/post/22980686843049)]
২. Ethereum ($ETH): অল্টসিজনের চাবিকাঠি
ইথারিয়াম $২,৫৫০ জোনে কনসোলিডেট করছে। এর RSI বর্তমানে ৪৩ এবং MACD নিউট্রাল জোনে অবস্থান করছে। এর মানে হলো পূর্ববর্তী র্যালির অতিরিক্ত হাইপ এখন ঠাণ্ডা হয়েছে এবং এটি বড় মুভমেন্টের জন্য প্রস্তুত হচ্ছে। বিশ্লেষকদের মতে, ETH/BTC পেয়ারের ব্রেকআউট নিশ্চিত হলেই অল্টকয়েনগুলোতে বড় র্যালি বা 'Altseason' শুরু হবে। [1, 2, 3]
৩. Binance Coin ($BNB): লাউঞ্চপুলের শক্তি
$৭৬৫+ মূল্যে ট্রেড হওয়া BNB চার্টে বেশ শক্তিশালী Binance Square Insights। এর RSI ৫৩-এর ঘরে থাকায় এটি স্পষ্ট বুলিশ মোমেন্টামে রয়েছে। MACD-তে ইতিবাচক হিস্টোগ্রাম দেখা যাচ্ছে, যা ইঙ্গিত করে যে বাইনান্স লাউঞ্চপুল এবং নতুন AI এজেন্ট ইন্টিগ্রেশনের কারণে হোল্ডাররা কয়েনটি ধরে রাখছেন [1.1.2, Binance Blog](https://www.binance.com/en/blog)।
৪. Solana ($SOL): নেটওয়ার্ক অ্যাক্টিভিটির জোয়ার
সোলাইনা বর্তমানে $১১৫.২০ লেভেলে অবস্থান করছে। RSI ৫৪.১২ (নিউট্রাল) হলেও MACD (১২, ২৬) একটি শক্তিশালী 'Buy' সিগন্যাল দিচ্ছে। ৯ই অক্টোবরের পরিকল্পিত মেইননেট আপগ্রেড (২০০ms স্লট) এবং অন-চেইন মেমকয়েন ভলিউমের কারণে ট্রেডাররা লং পজিশন নিতে আগ্রহী হচ্ছেন। $১২০-এর রেজিস্ট্যান্স ভাঙলে পরবর্তী টার্গেট $১৩৫+। [1, 2, 3, 4]
৫. Zcash ($ZEC): ইনস্টিটিউশনাল প্রেসার
প্রাইভেসি কয়েন Zcash Grayscale ETF-এর আউটফ্লোর কারণে সাময়িক চাপের মুখে রয়েছে। এর RSI এবং MACD উভয়ই ডাউনট্রেন্ড বা কনসোলিডেশন দেখাচ্ছে। তবে দীর্ঘমেয়াদী চার্টে বড় সাপোর্ট জোনে থাকায় নতুন বিনিয়োগকারীরা এটিকে ডিসিএ (DCA) করার সুযোগ হিসেবে দেখছেন।

 ট্রেডারদের জন্য এই সপ্তাহের কৌশল (Trading Strategy)
RSI ও MACD-এর কম্বিনেশন: শুধুমাত্র একটি ইন্ডিকেটর দেখে ট্রেড না করে, RSI যখন ওভারসোল্ড জোনে (<৩০) থাকবে এবং MACD যখন বুলিশ ক্রসওভার নিশ্চিত করবে, তখনই এন্ট্রি নেওয়া নিরাপদ।কঠোর স্টপ-লস: বর্তমান মার্কেটের ভোলাটিলিটি এড়াতে এবং বড় লস থেকে বাঁচতে সবসময় প্রপার রিস্ক-রিওয়ার্ড রেশিও মেনে স্টপ-লস ব্যবহার করুন। [1, [2](https://www.binance.com/en/square/post/17639474109170), [3](https://www.binance.com/en/square/post/22980686843049)]

title: 山寨季是怎么轮动的？为什么你的币总是最后一个涨
subTitle:
很多人难受的点：BTC涨的时候我的山寨不动，山寨起飞的时候我又没在
车上。其实山寨轮动是有大致剧本的。

【经典顺序】BTC先动（吸走注意力）→ 资金外溢到ETH和大主流 →
再扩散到板块龙头 → 最后扫到各种小币杂毛 → 全场普涨过热，行情
接近尾声。你总感觉自己的币最后涨，因为你买的位置往往就在轮动
链条的末端。

【两个实用观察】1. BTC占比（BTC.D）下降，通常说明资金在往山寨流，
山寨季启动的信号之一；2. 山寨普涨但BTC滞涨，往往是行情进入尾声
的信号，这时候追高杂毛币，接盘概率最大。

【结论】轮动不是平均主义，不是每个山寨都会涨。有叙事、有真实
流通量、有板块地位的才轮得到。与其猜哪个百倍币，不如盯紧资金
现在在哪、下一站可能去哪。

At the end of the chain.

📰 Why Hunter Biden’s LAPTOP Token Isn’t a Rug Pull, but “Trolling Trump”

Last week, Hunter Biden launched a spoof token called LAPTOP, sending the market into a frenzy. On the surface, it’s a joke—but behind it lies a jab at Trump. According to CoinTelegraph, when explaining his move, Hunter Biden said he was “maximally extracting value from Trump’s hype,” with the goal of poking fun at those “con artists” like Trump who love to hype. The news directly caused the token to explode immediately after listing, but it cooled down just as quickly.

Why is this news important?
This news matters because it reveals the surprising power of political gimmicks in the cryptocurrency market. Within less than 24 hours of launch, the LAPTOP token’s market cap surged past $10 million, setting a new record for the “fastest memecoin to explode.” What it reflects is the market’s frenzy for anything that can ignite social-media chatter—no matter how little real substance it has. Hunter Biden’s involvement turned the incident from simple parody into a marketing move with political attack overtones, and cross-over marketing like this often creates a massive impact on market sentiment.

The industry impact shows up mainly in three areas: first, it injects a new piece of “hype fuel” into the memecoin space, which in the short term could lift the prices of tokens with similar themes; second, this politicized operation has shown regulators the potential risks of crypto—when tokens are used for political promotion, it may trigger stricter oversight; and third, it also exposes the market’s disregard for the actual value of real projects, as investors seem more willing to buy into celebrities’ political statements.

Impact on the market
In the short term, the LAPTOP token’s surge could lift some memecoins tied to political figures—especially projects built around mockery or satire. But this effect won’t last long. Based on historical data, more than 90% of memecoins collapse within 72 hours after going viral. LAPTOP may follow the same pattern, because its rise depends more on social sentiment than on fundamentals.

The direct impact on BTC and ETH appears limited for now. BTC is struggling around the $80,000 level, while ETH has fallen below $2,400, and overall market sentiment remains bearish. At most, LAPTOP’s hype is a small, scattered spark that won’t change the bigger trend. However, if more political figures get involved with crypto, it could trigger a chain reaction from regulators and thus affect overall market sentiment.

Why is ignoring real project value a problem? Simply put: if investors always chase trends and celebrity effects, truly high-quality projects—with real technology and teams—may never get the attention or funding they deserve. It’s like a fairground full of people watching the spectacle, while the places worth learning from go unnoticed.

Trading/strategy idea
From my perspective, while the LAPTOP token may still have some “pulse” in the short term, the risk is extremely high. If market sentiment keeps shifting toward politicization, we may see more events like this—but the durability of this kind of hype usually doesn’t exceed two weeks. What’s more worth watching is whether regulators, prompted by this, intensify their scrutiny of celebrity tokens, which could spill over and hit the entire memecoin market.

Hold the BNB threshold at $724. If it breaks below that line, the memecoin celebration may really be over. If more political interference in crypto appears, this judgment becomes invalid.

📰 为什么 Hunter Biden 的 LAPTOP 代币不是跑路，而是"戏弄特朗普"？

亨特·拜登上周推出了一个叫 LAPTOP 的恶搞代币，引发市场轩然大波。表面上这是个笑话，但背后却暗藏对特朗普的嘲讽。据 CoinTelegraph 报道，亨特·拜登在解释这个行为时称，他是在"最大程度地榨取特朗普的炒作"，目的是戏弄那些像特朗普一样喜欢炒作的"骗局"。这件事直接导致了该代币上线即爆火，但很快又迅速冷却。

为什么这条新闻重要？
这条新闻之所以重要，是因为它揭示了政治噱头在加密货币市场中的惊人能量。LAPTOP 代币上线不到 24 小时，其市值就突破了 1000 万美元，创造了新的"最快 memecoin 爆炸"记录。这背后反映的是市场对任何能引爆社交媒体的话题的狂热追捧，哪怕这种追捧毫无实际基础。亨特·拜登的介入，让事件从单纯的恶搞升级为具有政治攻击意味的营销行为，这种跨界营销往往能制造出极强的市场情绪冲击。

对行业的影响主要体现在三个方面：首先，它为 memecoin 空间注入了新的炒作题材，短期内可能会带动类似题材的代币价格上涨；其次，这种政治化操作让监管机构看到了加密货币的潜在风险——当代币被用于政治宣传时，可能会引发更严格的监管；最后，它也暴露了市场对真实项目价值的忽视，投资者似乎更愿意为名人的政治表态买单。

对市场的影响
从短期来看，LAPTOP 代币的爆火可能会带动部分与政治人物相关的 memecoin 上涨，尤其是那些以嘲讽或调侃为主题的项目。但这个效应不会持续太久。根据历史数据，超过 90% 的 memecoin 在爆火后 72 小时内就会崩盘。LAPTOP 也可能会重蹈覆辙，因为其上涨主要依赖于社交情绪，而非基本面支撑。

对 BTC 和 ETH 的直接影响目前看有限。BTC 在 8 万美元关口承压，而 ETH 则跌破 2400 美元，市场整体情绪偏空。LAPTOP 的热度最多只能算是个零星小火花，不会改变大趋势。但如果出现更多政治人物介入加密货币的情况，可能会引发监管机构的连锁反应，从而影响整个市场情绪。

为什么说市场对真实项目价值的忽视是个问题？简单说：如果投资者永远只追逐热点和名人效应，那些真正有技术、有团队的优质项目可能永远得不到应有的关注和资金。这就像是在游乐场里看热闹的人挤满了头，而真正值得学习的地方却无人问津。

操作思路
从我的角度看，LAPTOP 代币虽然短期内可能还有脉冲空间，但风险极高。如果市场情绪继续向政治化倾斜，可能会看到更多类似事件，但这类炒作的持续性通常不超过两周。更值得关注的是，如果监管机构因此加强对名人代币的审查，可能会殃及整个 memecoin 市场。

守住 724 美元的 BNB 阈值，如果跌破这条线，memecoin 的狂欢可能真的要结束了。如果出现更多政治干预加密货币的情况，这个判断作废。

title: 滚仓：富贵险中求，还是爆仓加速器？
subTitle:
滚仓这个词最近很火，故事都一样：小本金几倍杠杆吃大趋势，滚动几次
翻几十倍。今天讲讲它没告诉你的部分。

【滚仓在干什么】浮盈不再落袋，而是当成新仓位的风险金继续开仓，
相当于拿市场的钱加杠杆。趋势不停，复利惊人；趋势一停，从浮盈
几十个点到归零，也就一两根大阴线的事。

【数学真相】滚仓的本质是「连续押对」。假设每次胜率60%，连对四次
的概率只有13%。你看到的一夜翻倍帖，背后是99个已经删号的人。
幸存者偏差是这个行业最贵的东西。

【如果你一定要试】1. 只用你亏光了也不心疼的那部分钱；2. 浮盈滚动
到一定倍数，强制抽出本金，用「市场的钱」继续滚；3. 提前写好清零
预案。滚仓是烟花，不是过日子。别拿过日子的钱，放烟花。

translatedData.title: Rolling over: seeking wealth in danger—or a crash-acceleration engine?
translatedData.subTitle:
“Rolling over” has been trending recently, and the story is always the same: a small amount of capital, a few times leverage to ride a big trend, then roll it
dozens of times, multiplying it by tens of times. Today, let’s talk about the parts it didn’t tell you.

【What rolling over is doing】The unrealized profit isn’t locked in; instead, it’s treated as margin for a new position to keep opening trades,
It’s like taking market money and adding leverage. The trend keeps going, and compounding is astonishing; once the trend stops,
points can drop to zero—just a couple of big bearish candles.

【The mathematical truth】The essence of “rolling over” is simply “continuously betting correctly.” Suppose you win with a 60% probability each time—then the chance of getting four in a row is
only 13%. The “overnight double” posts you see are backed by 99 people whose accounts have already been deleted.

🤔 Anyflo suddenly appeared out of nowhere and even bought a Sui project—why does this move have a subtle impact on the stablecoin payment landscape?

Anyflo has suddenly emerged from the “mysterious organization” in the crypto world. This time, it has renamed itself the Stablecoin Payments Coordination Company, and it has also acquired a team that builds Native projects for Sui. The company wants to try something new: it plans to hide the complex operations of blockchain—such as liquidity management and routing—behind the scenes, so that for enterprise users, using money feels as simple as using WeChat Pay. This move happened in Sui Basecamp, suggesting it wants to cut directly into the fast lane of Web3 payments.

Why is this news important?
At its core, Anyflo’s sudden arrival is the crypto industry looking for “profitable stablecoin use cases.” When traditional payment giants like PayPal started working on stablecoins, they were learning from OpenPay. Now Anyflo is directly building in the Sui ecosystem, which indicates that Sui’s tech stack (such as the Move language and the resource model) truly has advantages. Especially since it acquired the Native team, effectively pulling in Sui’s underlying development capabilities. That’s similar to how many other public chains are trying to grab DeFi users today. Why choose Sui? Because it’s fast and low-cost—well suited for high-frequency payment scenarios—making it complementary to Bitcoin’s slowness and Ethereum’s higher costs.

Market impact
For BTC and ETH, this news is somewhat neutral. If crypto can find more real-world payment scenarios like Anyflo’s and develop tools that help bring them to market, in theory it could boost use cases across the entire ecosystem. But to be fair, enterprise payments still rely mainly on USD stablecoins (such as USDC), and crypto stablecoins make up less than 5%. That means Anyflo wants to change the landscape, but the road ahead is long. Still, if in the future the Sui ecosystem is widely adopted by enterprises, it could—at least in theory—divert some Ethereum users (since ETH outside of DeFi and NFTs basically has little else to do). The more immediate effect is that Sui’s ecosystem activity might increase in the short term, but how long that effect can last remains unknown. Historically, similar events—like when Anchor launched—did indeed boost Solana’s TVL, but Sui is still much smaller in scale.

💡 Anyflo’s arrival suggests that stablecoin payments may move from the “developer playground” into the “enterprise trial” phase. But in the short term, it probably won’t cause any noticeable swings in BTC or ETH prices. If within the next six months Sui’s institutional adoption rate exceeds 20%, then this assessment would be invalid.

content:
🤔 Anyflo凭空出现还买了个Sui项目，为何这个动作对稳定币支付格局有微妙影响？

Anyflo突然从加密圈的"神秘组织"现身，这次改名叫稳定币支付协调公司，还买了做Sui项目Native的团队。这家公司想玩个新花样——把区块链的复杂操作（比如流动性管理、路由选择）全给企业用户藏起来，让企业觉得用钱就像用微信支付那么简单。此举发生在Sui Basecamp，说明它想直接插队Web3支付的快车道。

为什么这条新闻重要？
任何flo这家公司突然冒出来，本质是加密圈在找"能赚钱的稳定币用武之地"。传统支付巨头PayPal等开始搞Stablecoin时，都在学OpenPay。现在Anyflo直接做Sui生态，说明Sui的这套技术（比如Move语言和资源模型）确实有优势。特别是它收购Native团队，相当于直接把Sui的底层开发能力揽过来，这跟现在很多公链想抢DeFi用户有异曲同工之妙。为什么选Sui？因为Sui速度快、成本低，适合高频支付场景，这跟比特币的慢和以太坊的贵形成互补。

对市场的影响
对BTC和ETH来说，这个消息偏中性。如果加密货币能找到更多像Anyflo这样的支付场景落地工具，理论上能带动整个生态的用例。但话说回来，目前企业级支付还主要靠美元稳定币（比如USDC），加密稳定币占比不足5%。这意味着Anyflo想改变格局，道阻且长。不过，如果未来Sui生态能被企业广泛采用，理论上能分流一部分以太坊的用户（毕竟ETH除了DeFi和NFT基本没别的事可做）。更直接的影响是，Sui的生态活跃度可能会短期增加，但这个效果能持续多久还是未知数。历史上类似事件比如Anchor推出后，确实拉动了Solana的TVL，但Sui目前体量还小得多。

💡 Anyflo的出现意味着稳定币支付可能从"开发者玩"进入"企业试水"阶段。但短期看，它大概率不会让BTC或ETH价格出现明显波动。如果未来6个月内Sui的机构采用率超过20%，这个判断作废。

Why is this news important?

Impact on the market

But in the long run, it benefits the health of the entire industry, especially model companies that prioritize compliance. The regulatory environment will gradually become stricter—much like the gaming industry: early “rule-breakers” may ultimately be weeded out. Capital flows will increasingly favor companies with solid technology and data compliance. 📰 MSTR stock diluted and held back? Why a brighter Bitcoin outlook still can’t help

TD Cowen analyst keeps MSTR’s $260 price target, but highlights that shareholders will take bigger losses due to equity dilution. The software company making this prediction on Bitcoin is facing share price dilution risk—despite a positive outlook for Bitcoin. For investors, that’s a problem: when the market’s most favored asset price rises, returns from investing in MSTR get diluted.

Why this news matters
The key takeaway is an unintuitive phenomenon: industry leaders (like MSTR) benefit from the overall Bitcoin market boom, but equity dilution mechanisms in their governance structure are eroding shareholders’ real gains. The root cause is that MSTR’s earnings growth rate can’t fully keep pace with the speed of Bitcoin’s price rise, causing existing shareholders’ ownership percentages to keep shrinking after dilution. This also reflects a disconnect that may exist for some AI-prediction companies between short-term revenue growth and long-term valuation support.

Implications for the market
This serves as a reminder that even if Bitcoin keeps hitting new highs, investors still need to pay attention to the equity structure design at the company level. If companies like MSTR continue facing dilution pressure, it may trigger a reassessment of valuations across the entire AI-software/predictions industry. At present, MSTR’s stock performance is not strongly correlated with Bitcoin’s price trend (TD Cowen’s report does not mention correlation data, but notes dilution as the core contradiction).

Impact on the market
In the short term, this news could spark a sell-off of AI prediction companies like MSTR, because equity dilution directly harms shareholder interests. But in the long run, if Bitcoin continues to rise, these companies still have growth potential. The key is whether management can lift valuation through technological innovation. The impact on BTC/ETH is indirect, because dilution is fundamentally a governance issue rather than a shift in market sentiment or macro trends. This means investors need to revisit the valuation logic of AI prediction software—not simply equate rising Bitcoin with rising MSTR stock.

Historical parallels
Similar events have happened before—such as the 2008 financial crisis when banks faced equity dilution. Back then, share prices plunged while executives’ equity incentives were still being carried out, ultimately leading to even harsher losses for shareholders. This offers a reference point for MSTR’s current situation.

Trading/strategy considerations
I think MSTR’s stock may face near-term pressure, because equity dilution can fuel shareholder dissatisfaction. If Bitcoin’s price breaks above $85K and MSTR can deliver a more positive earnings report (e.g., revenue growth exceeding 50%), the stock could stabilize. But that view has invalidation conditions: if regulators begin conducting stricter scrutiny of AI prediction software, or if Bitcoin falls sharply to below $70K, the dilution issue could be overlooked by the market—instead, the stock price could swing significantly for other reasons.

📰 MSTR股价被稀释拖累？为什么比特币前景更亮了却帮不上忙

TD Cowen分析师维持MSTR $260价格目标，但强调股东因股权稀释将承受更大损失。这家预测比特币价格的软件公司，正面临股价被摊薄的风险，即便比特币前景向好。这对投资者来说是个问题：当市场最看好的资产价格上涨时，投资MSTR的回报却在被稀释。

为什么这条新闻重要？
这条新闻的关键在于揭示了一种反直觉现象：行业龙头企业（如MSTR）虽然受益于比特币市场的整体繁荣，但内部治理结构中的股权稀释机制正在削弱其股东的实际收益。根本原因在于，MSTR的盈利增长速度未能完全匹配比特币价格的上涨速度，导致原有股东的持股比例在摊薄后不断降低。这反映了部分AI预测公司可能存在的短期营收增长与长期估值支撑之间的脱节问题。

对市场的意义在于，它提醒投资者即使比特币价格持续创新高，也需要关注公司层面的股权结构设计。如果像MSTR这样的公司持续面临稀释压力，可能会引发对整个AI预测软件行业的估值重估。目前，MSTR股价表现与比特币价格走势的相关性并不强（TD Cowen的报告中未提及相关性数据，但指出稀释是核心矛盾）。

对市场的影响
短期看，这条新闻可能引发对MSTR类AI预测公司的抛售，因为股权稀释直接损害股东利益。但长期来看，如果比特币持续上涨，这类公司仍有增长潜力。关键在于管理层能否通过技术革新提升估值。对BTC/ETH的影响是间接的，因为稀释问题本质上是公司治理问题，而非市场情绪或宏观趋势变化。这意味着投资者需要重新审视AI预测软件的估值逻辑，而不是简单地将比特币上涨与MSTR股价上涨划等号。

历史上类似事件有2008年金融危机时银行股的股权稀释问题，当时股价暴跌但高管的股权激励仍在执行，最终导致更惨烈的股东损失。这为当前MSTR的情况提供了参考。

操作思路
我认为短期内MSTR股价可能承压，因为股权稀释会引发股东不满。如果未来比特币价格突破$85K且MSTR能给出更积极的财报（比如营收增速超过50%），股价或能企稳。但这个判断有失效条件：如果监管机构开始对AI预测软件进行严格审查，或比特币价格出现断崖式下跌至$70K以下，那么股权稀释问题可能被市场忽视，反而股价会因其他原因大幅波动。

title: 金字塔加仓：趋势单怎么越涨越加才不翻车
subTitle:
看对了趋势想加仓，怎么加？一上来就重仓+浮盈加满，是爆仓名单上的
常客。正确的做法叫金字塔加仓。

【原则】每次加仓的量比上一次少。比如首仓30%，第一次回调确认加20%，
再确认加10%。越往上仓位越轻，成本的重心压在低位，回调时你扛得住。

【反过来为什么危险】倒金字塔（底部轻仓、顶部越加越重）意味着你的
平均成本全在高位，稍微一回撤就由赚转亏，心态一崩，操作全变形。
很多人不是看错方向亏的钱，是加仓加错了顺序亏的钱。

【三条铁规矩】1. 只在盈利的单上加仓，亏损的单只减不加（不摊平！）；
2. 每加一次，整体止损位同步上移；3. 加仓前问自己：如果这是全新的一
笔钱，我现在还愿意在这个价位开仓吗？答案犹豫，就别加。

translatedData.title: Pyramiding: How to add to a trend trade the higher it rises without getting wrecked
translatedData.subTitle:
If you got the trend right and want to add to your position, how do you add? Jumping straight in with a heavy position and adding with full floating profit puts you on the list of accounts that get liquidated/face margin calls.
Regular customers. The correct approach is called pyramiding (adding to positions).

【Principle】 The amount you add each time should be less than the previous time. For example, if the first position is 30%, then after confirming the first pullback you add 20%,
Confirm again: add another 10%. The higher up you go, the lighter the position. The cost center of gravity stays at the lower levels, so when a pullback happens, you can withstand it.

【Why it’s dangerous the other way around】 An inverted pyramid (light positions at the bottom, adding heavier and heavier toward the top) means that your
average cost is all concentrated at the high end. Even a small retracement turns profit into loss; once your mindset breaks, your operations all get distorted.

title: 2%仓位法则：为什么亏得起才能活得久
subTitle:
今天讲一个被讲烂了但99%的人做不到的规矩：单笔交易的最大亏损，
不要超过总资金的2%。

【算笔账】1万U本金，2%就是单笔最多亏200U。连续错10次，还剩八千，
账户只回撤20%，靠几笔对的单就能回来。反过来，每次梭哈亏30%，
连错三次只剩34%，要翻近2倍才能回本——数学上已经基本判死刑了。

【怎么落地】不是「仓位不超过2%」，是「这笔单打到止损位时亏的钱
不超过2%」。所以正确顺序是：找止损位 → 算止损距离 → 反推仓位。
止损远的单仓位小，止损近的单仓位可以适当放大。

【为什么难】因为2%赚得太慢，人性嫌它不够刺激。但市场淘汰的从来
不是赚得慢的人，是亏得快的人。先做到不爆仓，再谈翻倍。

translatedData.title: The 2% Position Rule: Why You Can Only Survive Long by Being Able to Afford Loss
translatedData.subTitle:
Today I’ll talk about a rule that’s been talked to death but 99% of people can’t follow: the maximum loss per single trade,
should not exceed 2% of total capital.

【Do the math】 With a principal of 10,000 USDT (U), 2% means the maximum loss per trade is 200 U. After being wrong 10 times in a row, you have 8,000 left,
The account only draws down 20%. With just a few correct trades, it can come back. On the flip side, each time you go all-in and lose 30%,
After getting it wrong three times in a row, you're down to just 34%. You’d need to nearly double to break even—mathematically, it’s basically sentenced to death.

【How to implement】 It’s not “position size no more than 2%.” It’s “when this trade hits the stop-loss level, the money you lose is no more than 2%.” So the correct order is: find the stop-loss level → calculate the distance to the stop → infer the position size.
2%.” So the correct order is: find the stop-loss level → calculate the distance to the stop-loss → work backward to the position size.

📰 Just now, the government reportedly moved $101 million worth of BTC—now the action escalates: why might this unusual move make the market more cautious?

The U.S. Department of the Treasury suddenly transferred $101 million in Bitcoin from a wallet that was hacked at Bitfinex. It’s as if the government directly took the hackers’ stolen “black food” and put it back on the table. The news immediately startled the market—especially people using crypto as a safe-haven asset—who may wonder: is the government really getting serious about regulation this time?

South Korea is one of the most active crypto trading markets globally. Local capital withdrawing from the market → increased sell pressure on BTC. This move could shift regulatory expectations from “observation” to “intervention.”

Why is this news important?
This isn’t just a simple asset transfer—there are several deeper logics behind it. First, the government is finally “legalizing” stolen assets, which suggests that future handling of similar incidents may become more standardized. Second, the Treasury isn’t secretly operating in the background—it’s bringing the assets into the spotlight. That implies crypto assets may need to become more transparent going forward. Third, the government needs this money (possibly to replenish institutional investors’ accounts, according to CryptoBriefing), but choosing to act when the BTC price is already cut roughly in half actually looks like the government is sending a signal to the market: “You see, crypto is a tool, not a casino.”

Why call it “unusual”? Normally, the government might wait for prices to rebound before recovering the assets. But this time it acts proactively during a downturn. That suggests the policy “floor” may already be in place, but the regulatory boot is still on the way.

Impact on the market
In the short term, BTC/ETH may face downward pressure due to uncertainty. When the U.S. Treasury transfers assets back into its own wallet, it effectively labels the crypto market with “stronger regulation.” South Korea is one of the most active crypto trading markets worldwide—if local capital withdraws, the result is increased BTC sell pressure. If other institutional investors also panic, Bitcoin could keep falling. But in the medium to long term, if the government brings a large amount of BTC into the regulatory framework through this move, it could actually boost market confidence. For example, ETF inflows could directly support the BTC price, because institutional investors will know the government won’t allow those assets to be stolen by hackers again. Historically, there have been similar moves: back in 2017, Japan also recovered stolen Binance BTC, but that time it didn’t trigger major volatility. The unusual part this time is that the U.S. is a benchmark for global financial regulation, and its actions can directly influence other countries’ policies.

Trading/strategy takeaway
💡 This move doesn’t directly benefit or hurt BTC, but it suggests the government’s resolve to regulate crypto assets is strengthening. If, going forward, large-scale crypto assets are illicitly diverted, the U.S. government likely won’t ignore it. That means when the BTC price is below $60K, the likelihood of government intervention could rise significantly. If BTC breaks below $75K, this logic would no longer hold.

📰 刚说政府搬走1亿美元BTC，现在动作升级：为啥这次反常操作可能让市场更谨慎？

美国财政部突然把1.01亿美元的比特币从Bitfinex被盗钱包转走，相当于把黑客的黑菜直接拿回来当公菜。这条消息直接让市场吓了一跳，尤其是那些用加密当避险资产的人会想：政府这是要动真格监管了？韩国是全球加密交易最活跃市场之一，本土资金抽离→BTC抛压，这次操作可能让监管预期从"观察"升级到"干预"。

为什么这条新闻重要？
这条操作不是简单的资产转移，背后藏着几个深层逻辑。第一，政府终于把被盗资产"合法化"，意味着未来类似事件处理会更标准。第二，财政部不是在暗地操作，而是把资产拿到阳光下——这暗示加密资产未来可能要更透明。第三，政府需要这笔钱（据CryptoBriefing可能是为了补充机构投资者账户），但选在BTC价格腰斩时操作，反而像在给市场发信号："你看，加密资产是工具，不是赌场"。为什么说这反常？因为按常理，政府应该等价格反弹再回收，但这次在跌势中主动行动，说明政策底可能已经到位，但监管的靴子还在路上。

对市场的影响
短期来看，BTC/ETH可能会因为不确定性而承压。美国财政部把资产转移回自家钱包，相当于给加密市场贴了个"监管加强"的标签。韩国是全球加密交易最活跃市场之一，本土资金抽离→BTC抛压，如果其他机构投资者也跟着恐慌，比特币可能会继续跌。但中长期看，如果政府通过这次操作把大量BTC纳入监管体系，反而可能提升市场信心。比如ETF资金流入→直接支撑BTC价格，因为机构投资者知道政府不会让这些资产再被黑客拿走。历史上有类似操作，2017年时日本也回收了被盗币安的比特币，但那次没引发大波动——这次反常之处在于，美国是全球金融监管的标杆，他们的动作会直接影响其他国家的政策。

操作思路
💡 这次操作不直接利好或利空BTC，但意味着政府监管加密资产的决心在增强。如果未来出现大规模加密货币被非法挪用的情况，美国政府可能不会坐视不理。这意味着BTC价格在$60K以下时，政府干预的可能性会显著增加。如果跌破$75K这条逻辑就不成立。本文无任何项目方赞助，作者不持有文中提及标的。

title: 分批止盈：落袋为安和让利润奔跑，怎么兼得
subTitle:
止盈比止损难，因为止损砍的是恐惧，止盈砍的是贪婪。行情越好你越不想
卖，一回调又后悔没跑。分享我一直在用的分批止盈。

【三段式】第一段：到第一个目标位（比如1倍盈亏比）减仓1/3，先落袋，
这时候这笔单已经不会亏了，心态立刻不一样。第二段：到第二目标位
（比如2倍盈亏比）再减1/3。第三段：剩下的用移动止损跟，跌破均线
或前低就走，让利润自己跑。

【为什么这样】全仓跑早了会拍大腿，全仓拿着经常坐电梯回到解放前。
分批的本质是把「卖在最高点」这个不可能任务，拆成三笔还不错的决策。

【关键动作】减仓之后把止损上移到成本价，这就是传说中的「免费单」。
手里的利润单，最怕的就是抱着抱着变成亏损单。

translatedData.title: Batch-wise Take-Profit: Take profits to be safe and let profits run—how to have both
translatedData.subTitle:
Take-profit is harder than stop-loss, because the stop-loss cuts off fear, while the take-profit cuts off greed. The better the market is, the less you want to...
sell. The moment it pulls back, you regret not selling earlier. I’m sharing the batch-wise take-profit method I’ve been using.

[Three-stage] First segment: when it reaches the first target level (for example, 1x risk-reward), reduce the position by 1/3, take some profits off the table,...
At this point, this trade won’t lose money anymore, and my mindset instantly changes. Second segment: when it reaches the second target level...
(For example, 2x the risk-reward ratio) minus 1/3. Third segment: the remaining position uses a trailing stop, and if it breaks below the moving average...
or the previous low, then exit and let the profit run by itself.

[Why this way] Going all-in and exiting too early will make you slap your forehead. Holding all-in often means you ride an elevator back to the days of going back to square one.

title: 止损到底该挂哪？技术位和百分比，我这样选
subTitle:
止损挂在哪儿，比设不设止损更讲究。挂太近天天被扫，挂太远一次亏麻。

【固定百分比法】比如每次亏本金的1%-2%就离场。简单粗暴，适合新手
建立纪律。缺点是不看结构，可能正好挂在别人的止损堆里。

【技术位止损法】挂在结构失效的位置：做多挂关键支撑下方，做空挂
压力位上方。逻辑是——这个位置破了，说明我看错的证据出现了。
配合仓位反推：止损距离大，就把仓位调小，保证单笔亏损还是本金的
1%-2%。这才是「止损位定仓位」的正确顺序。

【我最常用的组合】技术位定方向失效点，仓位保命。两者一合并，你
会发现：止损宽的交易，仓位自然就该小；止损近的交易才能放大点仓位。
顺序千万别反——先定仓位再找止损，是大多数人亏钱的根源。
